Why is this called Zero-shot Prompting?

They should answer:

Because we only gave the model an instruction.
 We did not provide any examples of reviews and their expected outputs.
 
 Request :
 {
    "review":"Battery backup is amazing and the camera quality is excellent."
}

Response :

{
    "review": "Battery backup is amazing and the camera quality is excellent.",
    "sentiment": "Generated by AI",
    "explanation": "1. Sentiment: Positive\n2. One-line explanation: The reviewer praises both the battery backup and camera quality, indicating a high level of satisfaction."
}
Request :
{
    "review":"Waste of money"
}
Response :
{
    "review": "Waste of money",
    "sentiment": "Generated by AI",
    "explanation": "1. Sentiment: Negative\n2. One-line explanation: The customer expresses dissatisfaction with the product, indicating it was not worth the cost."
}
-------------------
With improved response
{
    "review": "Battery backup is amazing and the camera quality is excellent.",
    "sentiment": "Positive",
    "explanation": "The review highlights satisfaction with both the battery backup and camera quality."
}

----

Zero-shot Prompting: We give the model only instructions. No examples are provided.
One-shot Prompting: We give the model instructions + one example (input and expected output).
Few-shot Prompting: We give the model instructions + multiple examples (inputs and expected outputs) to guide the response.

A one-line summary for students:

The difference between Zero-shot, One-shot, and Few-shot is not the code—it is the number of examples included in the prompt.
